title: Proper direct image, base change and projection formula for finite coefficients
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring killed by a power of $\ell$, and $p\colon X\to Y$ proper
between standing schemes.

1. $Rp_*$ maps $\Dctf(X,A)$ into $\Dctf(Y,A)$.
2. For a cartesian square with $g\colon Y'\to Y$, the base change map
   $g^*Rp_*K\to Rp'_*g'^*K$ is an isomorphism in $D(Y'_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$ for $K\in\Dctf(X,A)$.
3. For $K\in\Dctf(X,A)$ and $M\in\Dctf(Y,A)$ the projection formula map
   $Rp_*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_AM\to Rp_*(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_Ap^*M)$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Identify coefficients and choose étale antecedents. Give the finite ring $A$ its discrete topology. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-condensed-ring-constant] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-ring-constant], its pulled-back condensed ring on every scheme $T$ is the constant ring sheaf $A_T$; transport module structures along this ring isomorphism throughout. The standing schemes are separated and finite type over the field of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], hence qcqs. The ring $A$ is Noetherian: every ideal is a finite set and is generated by its elements. Thus [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] applies. Choose $K_0\in D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ and, when needed, $M_0\in D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(Y_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ with $\nu_X^*K_0\simeq K$ and $\nu_Y^*M_0\simeq M$. Their Tor intervals are also intervals for $K,M$, and conversely. Since $K\in\Dbc(X,A)$ it is bounded, in particular bounded below, and each cohomology sheaf $H^q(K)$ lies in $\Cons(X,A)$; as $X$ is qcqs and $A$ is discrete Noetherian, [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] says that every such constructible pro-étale $A_X$-module sheaf is classical, so $K$ is a classical complex. Its abelian cohomology sheaves are $A_X$-modules, hence annihilated by the same power of $\ell$ that annihilates $A$.

source.place: Transport paragraph; finite discrete coefficient identifications; finite-Tor comparison

proof.text: Choose a uniform geometric fibre dimension bound. Properness makes $p$ finite type, and $Y$ is quasi-compact by the standing setting. By [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound] there is $e\geq0$ with $\dim X_y\leq e$ for every scheme-theoretic fibre. For any geometric point $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$, $X_{\bar y}$ is the base change of $X_y$ along the field extension $\kappa(y)\to\Omega$. The fibre projection is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], so these fibres are finite type over their respective fields. The field-extension clause of [lem-kun-dimension-extension] gives $\dim X_{\bar y}=\dim X_y\leq e$. Empty fibres are allowed.

source.place: Tag 0A3V, lemma-morphism-finite-type-bounded-dimension; Tag 01W4, lemma-base-change-proper; field extension via algebra.tex Tag 00P3

proof.text: The integer $c=2e$ is a uniform $\ell$-cohomological bound for these geometric fibres. The field $\Omega$ is algebraically closed, hence separably closed; [lem-kun-cd-sep-closed-point] gives torsion cohomological dimension zero. For every nonempty $X_{\bar y}$, apply [thm-sc-finite-type-torsion-cd] over $\Omega$: its torsion cohomological dimension is at most $2\dim X_{\bar y}\leq2e$. For an empty fibre every sheaf and every cohomology group is zero, so the same nonnegative bound works. In particular the bound holds for $\ell$-power torsion sheaves, which are a subclass of the torsion sheaves.

source.place: Paragraph (1), uniform finite cohomological bound (Stacks 0F10); explicit geometric-fibre bound

proof.text:
Prove (1), checking the current hypotheses of [det-ctf-finite-proper-tor]. By [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], the same field $k$ has positive characteristic different from $\ell$, $X,Y$ are separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and $p$ is a proper $k$-morphism. Choose $r\ge1$ with $\ell^rA=0$, enlarging the annihilating exponent if necessary; this also covers $A=0$. Step 1 gives an antecedent $K_0$ in the ordinary small-étale category $D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ with constant coefficients. Choose integers $a\le b$ and a Tor interval $[a,b]$ for $K_0$, as allowed by its finite Tor amplitude. All these categories have the ordinary, uncompleted constant $A$-module coefficients required by the cited lemma; the coefficient identifications of step 1 are used before this application. Set the cited lemma's $d=c=2e\ge0$; its geometric fibre $X_{\bar y}$ is exactly the base change treated in steps 2-3, not a fibre over the unextended residue field. Step 3 gives its required vanishing for every $\ell$-power torsion abelian sheaf on every geometric fibre, where each local section may be killed by its own power of $\ell$; a single global annihilating exponent for these test sheaves is not assumed. Thus [det-ctf-finite-proper-tor], with its morphism $p_X=p$ and $C=K_0$, gives that $Rp_{\mathrm{ét},*}K_0$ is bounded constructible of Tor amplitude $[a,b+c]$. Since $p$ is proper, it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] identifies
$$Rp_{\mathrm{proét},*}K\simeq\nu_Y^*Rp_{\mathrm{ét},*}K_0.$$
Now [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] on $Y$ transfers bounded constructibility and that Tor interval. Hence $Rp_*K\in\Dctf(Y,A)$.

source.place: Paragraph (1); finite-proper Tor argument realized by the current corrected statement of det-ctf-finite-proper-tor, with its standing setting and sectionwise ell-power torsion hypotheses checked explicitly

proof.text: Prove (2). Step 1 verifies exactly the input hypotheses of [sk-thm-properbasechange]: $A$ is a commutative ring and $K$ is a bounded-below classical complex with torsion abelian cohomology. That node already states that the canonical pro-étale exchange $g^*Rp_*K\to Rp'_*g'^*K$ is an isomorphism for an arbitrary $g$. Thus it gives the required map in the ambient derived category of $Y'_{\mathrm{proét}}$; no constructibility or finite-Tor assertion on the pullback is needed. In particular $g$ is not required to be proper, smooth or flat.

source.place: Paragraph (2); use the current classical pro-étale statement of sk-thm-properbasechange

proof.text: Verify the bounded-below hypothesis needed when comparing the tensor input in (3). Keep the ordered Tor interval $a\le b$ for $K_0$ from step 4, and choose integers $r\le s$ giving a Tor interval for $M_0$, which exists by step 1. By [lem-sf-etale-flat-model], choose flat complexes $P,Q$ representing $K_0,M_0$ and zero outside $[a,b]$ and $[r,s]$, respectively. These bounded-above flat complexes are K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. For the ringed-topos morphism $p_{\mathrm{ét}}$ with constant coefficient rings, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] says that $p^*Q$ is K-flat with flat terms. Since the coefficient structural map is the constant-ring isomorphism, pullback is exact, applies termwise and does not change the range $[r,s]$. Consequently the total tensor $P\otimes_Ap^*Q$ computes $K_0\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}p^*M_0$ and is zero outside $[a+r,b+s]$: a degree-$n$ summand requires $i\in[a,b]$, $j\in[r,s]$ and $i+j=n$. Thus this input is bounded below, even when $A$ has infinite global dimension.

source.place: Paragraph (3), bounded-below finite-Tor inputs; Stacks 06YQ and 07A4 for flat models and tensor pullback

proof.text:
On the étale site, [lem-kun-0f0g] applies because $p$ is proper and $A$ is a torsion ring ($\ell^n1_A=0$ for some $n$). It gives the canonical isomorphism
$$\pi_{\mathrm{ét}}:Rp_{\mathrm{ét},*}K_0\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M_0\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_{\mathrm{ét},*}(K_0\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}p_{\mathrm{ét}}^*M_0).$$
Here the map is the projection morphism of [def-kun-projection-formula-map], namely the adjunct of the tensor comparison followed by $\varepsilon_{K_0}\otimes1$. This cited theorem holds on unbounded derived categories, so the bounded complexes here are legitimate inputs without an extra coefficient-ring regularity assumption.

Identify the map in (3), not just its source and target. For every scheme $T$ write $F_T=\nu_T^*$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to $\nu_T$, with structural ring map the identity onto the pulled-back constant ring. It gives the canonical comparison $F_T(U\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}V)\simeq F_TU\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}F_TV$. By [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison], $p_{\mathrm{proét}}^*F_Y\simeq F_Xp_{\mathrm{ét}}^*$ and $F_YRp_{\mathrm{ét},*}\simeq Rp_{\mathrm{proét},*}F_X$, compatibly with the units and counits. The latter comparison is available at both $K_0$ and $K_0\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}p^*M_0$ by steps 1 and 6. These isomorphisms turn $F_Y(\pi_{\mathrm{ét}})$ into an arrow with the source and target of (3). To check it is the canonical arrow, transpose under $p_{\mathrm{proét}}^*\dashv Rp_{\mathrm{proét},*}$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. The transported transpose is
$$p_{\mathrm{proét}}^*(Rp_{\mathrm{proét},*}K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M)\simeq p_{\mathrm{proét}}^*Rp_{\mathrm{proét},*}K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}p_{\mathrm{proét}}^*M\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_K\otimes1}K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}p_{\mathrm{proét}}^*M.$$
Indeed the counit is the one specified by direct-image comparison, and the two tensor/pullback identifications agree: on flat representatives both are the sheaf pullback of the same balanced tensor map $x\otimes y\mapsto x\otimes y$ in each bidegree, so their total complexes have identical component maps and signs. By the adjunction bijection this is exactly the canonical projection-formula arrow. A functor sends an isomorphism and its inverse to inverse arrows, so $F_Y(\pi_{\mathrm{ét}})$ is invertible. Conjugating by the displayed comparison isomorphisms proves (3).

source.place: Paragraph (3), transport via comparison; Stacks 09A6, 07A4 and 0F0G; explicit counit-mate calculation
